label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Big news (please read this before Thanksgiving, Dad especially)

Ok. Deep breath. I've been sitting on this for a few weeks and I want you all to hear it from me before it turns into a whole thing over the turkey.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real business now, with an LLC and a website and everything. I'm officially a self-employed wedding photographer.

Here's how it happened. On October 6th Marisol told me she was closing Rosebud Lane at the end of October. I've shot for her for four years, so that was a lot to take in. The studio closed at the end of the month like she said. I'll be honest, the first couple days I mostly stared at the wall.

Then I realized I'd been planning for this exact moment in my head for about two years. I've kept a running list on my phone of what I'd name it, what I'd charge, which lenses I'd need, all of it. So this isn't me panicking and jumping off a cliff. It's me finally doing the thing I've been quietly getting ready for, just a little sooner than I expected.

**Before anyone asks, here's where things actually stand:**

- I filed the LLC on October 22nd. I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer, and I cried a little. Not sad crying, more like "oh wow I just did that" crying. A guy pushing a cart full of paper towels definitely saw me. Fernhollow Photo LLC is real.
- The website went live November 1st.
- **I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027.** Six of those couples came to me through Marisol, and eight found me on their own. June is my busiest month with four weddings, and the furthest one is all the way out at Wallowa Lake in September. (Road trip, anyone?)
- Deposits are already coming in.
- For the big weddings I'll have Jae second shooting with me, paid per wedding. Jae is great and I trust them completely, so I'm not trying to do 300 person weddings alone.

**Dad, this next part is for you. Everyone else can read it too:**

I have health insurance. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5th and it starts January 1st. There's no gap and I'm not going without. You can skip the speech at Ruthie's. I know you love the speech. I know you've had the school portrait thing ready to go since August. I love you and I appreciate it, and I promise I've thought about it.

**The best part:**

A couple weeks ago I got an email from Dahlia and Ken. They're getting married June 12th at Timberline Lodge, and they booked me because they saw the photos I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls. That's my first booking that was 100% mine. They didn't come through a referral or the studio, they just saw my work and wanted me. I read that email maybe eleven times. Sam had to take my phone away.

Speaking of Sam, he made me a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW, with one L. He swears the cake was too small for the second one. We ate it anyway and it was delicious, and honestly a cake with a typo is the most fitting way this could have started.

**About Marisol:**

I really have to say this. Pretty much everything I know about this job, I learned from Marisol. She taught me how to read a room, how to get Uncle So-and-so to actually smile in the group photo, how to keep a bride calm when it starts pouring rain twenty minutes before the ceremony, and how to do my own taxes without crying (mostly). When she told me about the studio, one of the first things she did was start sending her 2027 couples my way. She told me I was ready. Apparently she's thought that for a while. I wouldn't be doing any of this without her, and I hope she knows how much that means to me.

**And Grandma, this part is for you:**

I'm not sure everybody knows where the name comes from. Fernhollow is the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, with Grandma's Pentax, which was way too heavy for me and which I was definitely not supposed to be carrying around by myself. I remember the light coming down through the trees and thinking I had to figure out how to keep it. I've basically been chasing that ever since.

So Grandma, the name is for you. You handed me that camera and here we are. Thank you.

**Is it scary?**

Yes, obviously. I'm 32 and I just walked away from steady work to run my own business in an industry where people book a year and a half ahead. Some days I'm so excited I can't sleep, and some days I lie there doing math in my head. Both are true. But I have a plan, I have a full calendar for next year, I have insurance (DAD), and I have a lot of people in my corner. Mostly what I feel right now is excited, and I'd really love for you all to be excited with me.

**Now, a Thanksgiving offer:**

I'm bringing the camera to Ruthie's on the 26th. If anyone wants family pictures, like your own household, couples, kids, grandkids, whatever you want, I'll take them for free. Holiday cards are coming, people. Grab me sometime before or after dinner while the light's still decent. Bree, I'd love to get a few of Juniper if you're up for it, no pressure at all, and I'll wash my hands a lot. And yes, I'll do the big group photo too. Uncle Greg, wear a warmer coat this year.

Mom, I'm bringing rolls and the cranberry thing. And yes, Sam is coming. He's driving so I can nap on the way down.

If you want to see what I've been working on, the website is up. I'll put the link in the comments. Feel free to send it to anyone you know who's getting married. A cousin of a coworker, your neighbor's daughter, whoever. Word of mouth is basically my whole marketing plan right now. I'm kidding. Mostly.

Love you all so much. Thanks for always being the people who show up. See you on the 26th, and come find me with your questions. Questions are welcome. Lectures, slightly less.

Tessa
(owner and sole employee of Fernhollow Photo LLC, which is still a wild thing to type)
